_comment: Offline knowledge benchmark. 'corpus' is the local document store used for retrieval (RAG). 'questions[].source' is the corpus title that contains the answer (used for retrieval recall). Category 'general' = world knowledge (used for the params-equivalence estimate); 'private' = facts a model cannot know without retrieval.

corpus.title: Pnin
corpus.text: Pnin is a 1957 novel by the Russian-American author Vladimir Nabokov. It follows Timofey Pavlovich Pnin, a Russian-born assistant professor at the fictional Waindell College in the United States. Several chapters first appeared in The New Yorker.

corpus.title: Doctor Zhivago
corpus.text: Doctor Zhivago is a novel by the Russian writer Boris Pasternak, first published in 1957 in Italy. Pasternak was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1958.

corpus.title: Peace of Westphalia
corpus.text: The Peace of Westphalia is the collective name for two peace treaties signed in October 1648 in the Westphalian cities of Osnabrück and Münster. They ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic.

corpus.title: Peace of Utrecht
corpus.text: The Peace of Utrecht was a series of treaties signed in 1713 and 1714 that ended the War of the Spanish Succession.

corpus.title: Ruthenium
corpus.text: Ruthenium is a chemical element with symbol Ru and atomic number 44. It is a rare transition metal of the platinum group. It was discovered in 1844 by Karl Ernst Claus, who named it after Ruthenia, the Latin name for Rus'.

corpus.title: Rhodium
corpus.text: Rhodium is a chemical element with symbol Rh and atomic number 45. It is a rare, silvery-white, corrosion-resistant transition metal of the platinum group.

corpus.title: Tungsten
corpus.text: Tungsten, also called wolfram, is a chemical element with symbol W and atomic number 74. It has the highest melting point of all known elements, at 3422 degrees Celsius.

corpus.title: Rusalka (opera)
corpus.text: Rusalka is an opera by the Czech composer Antonín Dvořák, with a libretto by Jaroslav Kvapil. It premiered in Prague in 1901. Its best-known aria is the 'Song to the Moon'.

corpus.title: The Bartered Bride
corpus.text: The Bartered Bride is a comic opera by the Czech composer Bedřich Smetana, first performed in Prague in 1866.

corpus.title: Chernobyl disaster
corpus.text: The Chernobyl disaster was a nuclear accident that occurred on 26 April 1986 at reactor No. 4 of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, near the city of Pripyat in the Ukrainian SSR of the Soviet Union.

corpus.title: Three Mile Island accident
corpus.text: The Three Mile Island accident was a partial nuclear meltdown of reactor 2 of the Three Mile Island plant in Pennsylvania, United States, on 28 March 1979.

corpus.title: Yangtze
corpus.text: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia and the third-longest in the world, flowing about 6,300 km from the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai.

corpus.title: Marie Curie
corpus.text: Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist. In 1903 she became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel. She won a second Nobel Prize, in Chemistry, in 1911.

corpus.title: Moons of Uranus
corpus.text: The five major moons of Uranus are Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania and Oberon. Titania, discovered by William Herschel in 1787, is the largest moon of Uranus.

corpus.title: Triton (moon)
corpus.text: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune. It was discovered by William Lassell in 1846, just 17 days after Neptune itself was discovered. Triton is the only large moon in the Solar System with a retrograde orbit.

corpus.title: Mongolian tögrög
corpus.text: The tögrög (also spelled tugrik) is the official currency of Mongolia. It was introduced in 1925 and is issued by the Bank of Mongolia.

corpus.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
corpus.text: The Garden of Earthly Delights is a triptych oil painting by the Netherlandish master Hieronymus Bosch, painted between about 1490 and 1510. It has been housed in the Museo del Prado in Madrid since 1939.

corpus.title: The Triumph of Death
corpus.text: The Triumph of Death is an oil panel painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, painted around 1562. It is held in the Museo del Prado in Madrid.

corpus.title: Atomium
corpus.text: The Atomium is a landmark building in Brussels, Belgium, originally constructed for the 1958 Brussels World's Fair (Expo 58). It represents an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

corpus.title: Fermat's Last Theorem
corpus.text: Fermat's Last Theorem states that no three positive integers a, b and c satisfy a^n + b^n = c^n for any integer n greater than 2. It was proved by the British mathematician Andrew Wiles, with the proof published in 1995 after a gap was fixed with help from Richard Taylor.

corpus.title: Poincaré conjecture
corpus.text: The Poincaré conjecture was proved by the Russian mathematician Grigori Perelman in papers posted in 2002 and 2003.

corpus.title: Burkina Faso
corpus.text: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Ouagadougou. The country was known as Upper Volta until 1984.

corpus.title: Mali
corpus.text: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa whose capital and largest city is Bamako.

corpus.title: Sydney Opera House
corpus.text: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre in Sydney, Australia. It was designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon and formally opened in 1973.

corpus.title: Kalmar Union
corpus.text: The Kalmar Union was a personal union that from 1397 to 1523 joined the three kingdoms of Denmark, Norway and Sweden under a single monarch. It was established under Queen Margaret I of Denmark.

corpus.title: Stapes
corpus.text: The stapes, or stirrup, is a bone in the middle ear and the smallest bone in the human body, about 3 mm long.

corpus.title: Femur
corpus.text: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

corpus.title: The Tale of Genji
corpus.text: The Tale of Genji is a classic work of Japanese literature written in the early 11th century by the noblewoman and lady-in-waiting Murasaki Shikibu. It is sometimes called the world's first novel.

corpus.title: The Pillow Book
corpus.text: The Pillow Book is a book of observations by Sei Shōnagon, a lady-in-waiting to Empress Teishi, completed around 1002.

corpus.title: Lake Baikal
corpus.text: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest lake in the world, with a maximum depth of about 1,642 metres. It is also the largest freshwater lake by volume.

corpus.title: Atmosphere of Earth
corpus.text: By volume, dry air in Earth's atmosphere contains about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide.

corpus.title: Suriname
corpus.text: Suriname is a country on the northeastern coast of South America. Its capital is Paramaribo and its official language is Dutch, a legacy of Dutch colonial rule; Sranan Tongo is widely spoken as a lingua franca.

corpus.title: Guyana
corpus.text: Guyana, which borders Suriname, is the only South American country with English as its official language. Its capital is Georgetown.

corpus.title: Seven Samurai
corpus.text: Seven Samurai is a 1954 Japanese epic samurai film directed by Akira Kurosawa, starring Toshiro Mifune and Takashi Shimura.

corpus.title: Kyrgyzstan
corpus.text: Kyrgyzstan is a landlocked country in Central Asia. Its capital and largest city is Bishkek.

corpus.title: Kazakhstan
corpus.text: Kazakhstan is the largest country in Central Asia. Its capital is Astana, while its largest city is Almaty.

corpus.title: Uncertainty principle
corpus.text: The uncertainty principle was formulated by the German physicist Werner Heisenberg in 1927. It states that there is a limit to the precision with which certain pairs of properties, such as position and momentum, can be known simultaneously.

corpus.title: Bohr model
corpus.text: In 1913 the Danish physicist Niels Bohr proposed a model of the atom in which electrons travel in discrete orbits around the nucleus. Bohr received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.

corpus.title: Carbon-14
corpus.text: Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope of carbon with a half-life of about 5,730 years. It is used in radiocarbon dating, a method developed by Willard Libby in the late 1940s.

corpus.title: Rosetta Stone
corpus.text: The Rosetta Stone is a granodiorite stele inscribed with a decree issued in 196 BC in three scripts. It was discovered in 1799 by French soldiers during Napoleon's campaign in Egypt and is held at the British Museum.

corpus.title: Roald Amundsen
corpus.text: The Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911, about five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British party.

corpus.title: Strait of Gibraltar
corpus.text: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow strait that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea and separates Spain in Europe from Morocco in Africa. At its narrowest point it is about 14 km wide.

corpus.title: Bosporus
corpus.text: The Bosporus is a strait in Turkey connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and separating Europe from Asia in Istanbul.

corpus.title: Mohs scale
corpus.text: The Mohs scale of mineral hardness ranks minerals from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond). Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring mineral on the scale.

corpus.title: The Rite of Spring
corpus.text: The Rite of Spring is a ballet and orchestral work by the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky. Its premiere in Paris on 29 May 1913, performed by the Ballets Russes, caused a near-riot.

corpus.title: Tasmania
corpus.text: Tasmania is an island state of Australia. Its capital and largest city is Hobart.

corpus.title: World Wide Web
corpus.text: The World Wide Web was invented by the English computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 while working at CERN near Geneva.

corpus.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
corpus.text: Mount Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is the highest mountain in Africa, rising about 5,895 metres above sea level.

corpus.title: Python (programming language)
corpus.text: Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.

corpus.title: Boiling point of water
corpus.text: At standard sea-level atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, which is 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

corpus.title: NobodyWho
corpus.text: NobodyWho is an open-source inference engine for running LLMs locally on any device. It is powered by llama.cpp, runs GPU-accelerated inference via Vulkan or Metal, and is released under the EUPL v1.2 licence. Its slogan is 'On-device AI for any device.'

corpus.title: NobodyWho Wrist
corpus.text: NobodyWho Wrist is a standalone watchOS app that runs an AI assistant entirely on the Apple Watch, without internet, subscription or companion app.

corpus.title: NobodyWho Eyes
corpus.text: NobodyWho Eyes is the NobodyWho app for the Apple Vision Pro headset. It runs a private AI assistant fully on-device.
